title: C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 13 suppresses osteoclast differentiation via interference with RANKL-RANK interaction.
authors: Ho, Trung-Loc; Lee, Kun-Tsan; He, Yu-Hao; Thuong, Le Huynh Hoai; Achudhan, David; Huang, Wei-Chien; Ko, Chih-Yuan; Liu, Chun-Lin; Guo, Jeng-Hung; Tang, Chih-Hsin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CXCL13通过干扰RANKL-RANK蛋白互作抑制破骨细胞分化，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作与分子对接，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且方法以湿实验为主，仅分子对接为辅助，与TF-DNA结合建模课题关联度低。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Osteoclastogenesis, the differentiation of osteoclasts from monocyte/macrophage precursors, is essential for physiological bone remodeling but contributes to pathological bone loss in arthritis, osteoporosis, and bone metastasis when dysregulated. CXCL13 is a CXC chemokine well recognized for its role in immune regulation; however, its function in osteoclast biology remains undefined. This study aimed to investigate the effects of CXCL13 on RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis. METHODS: RAW264.7 cells were stimulated with RANKL to induce osteoclastogenesis. Osteoclast formation was evaluated by TRAP and F-actin ring staining, and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR). GEO bioinformatic analysis revealed gene expression changes during RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis. Mature osteoclast apoptosis was analyzed by cleaved caspase-3 immunofluorescence staining. MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling activation was examined by Western blotting and NF-kappaB luciferase reporter assays. Molecular docking and co-immunoprecipitation were performed to evaluate the interaction between CXCL13 and RANK. RESULTS: CXCL13 inhibited RANKL-induced osteoclast formation, suppressed osteoclast marker expression, disrupted F-actin ring assembly, and promoted apoptosis in mature osteoclasts. Mechanistically, CXCL13 attenuated MAPK and NF-kappaB activation and blocked p65 nuclear translocation in a CXCR5-independent manner by competitively interfering with RANKL-RANK binding and downstream RANK-TRAF6 signaling. DISCUSSION: These findings identify CXCL13 as a novel suppressor of osteoclastogenesis by interfering with RANKL-RANK signaling, unveiling an unrecognized regulatory role in osteoclast biology and suggesting potential therapeutic relevance for bone loss disorders.
abstract_zh: 引言：破骨细胞生成（osteoclastogenesis），即单核细胞/巨噬细胞前体分化为破骨细胞的过程，对于生理性骨重塑至关重要，但在关节炎、骨质疏松症和骨转移中若失调，则会导致病理性骨丢失。CXCL13是一种CXC趋化因子，因其在免疫调节中的作用而广为人知；然而，其在破骨细胞生物学中的功能尚未明确。本研究旨在探讨CXCL13对RANKL诱导的破骨细胞生成的影响。方法：用RANKL刺激RAW264.7细胞以诱导破骨细胞生成。通过TRAP和F-actin环染色以及定量实时PCR（qPCR）评估破骨细胞形成。GEO生物信息学分析揭示了RANKL诱导破骨细胞生成过程中的基因表达变化。通过cleaved caspase-3免疫荧光染色分析成熟破骨细胞凋亡。通过Western blotting和NF-kappaB荧光素酶报告基因实验检测MAPK和NF-kappaB信号通路激活。采用分子对接和免疫共沉淀评估CXCL13与RANK之间的相互作用。结果：CXCL13抑制了RANKL诱导的破骨细胞形成，抑制了破骨细胞标志物表达，破坏了F-actin环组装，并促进了成熟破骨细胞的凋亡。机制上，CXCL13以不依赖CXCR5的方式，通过竞争性干扰RANKL-RANK结合及下游RANK-TRAF6信号传导，减弱了MAPK和NF-kappaB的激活，并阻断了p65核转位。讨论：这些发现将CXCL13鉴定为通过干扰RANKL-RANK信号传导抑制破骨细胞生成的新型抑制因子，揭示了其在破骨细胞生物学中未被认识的调控作用，并为骨丢失疾病提供了潜在的治疗相关性。
